rv.q: If the production is uneven, well, so is the play.
Everything technically works, but there's also the persistent deflation that comes with missed potential.
This version only runs through August 23, so get your free tickets while you can.
Director Daniel Sullivan’s production, however, is done with enough intelligence and conviction to make a strong case for it as one of the Bard’s masterpieces.
Old as time but still invigorating — the three hours and 20 minutes flies by, evoking many laughs, some gasps and even a few whoops from the audience.
It's a bit of a muddle, to be honest, and this production revels in its messiness in ways that both captivate and frustrate.

cn.t: Daniel Sullivan's traditional production of "The Winter's Tale" earns praise for its spirited staging and powerful performances, particularly from Lily Rabe and Raúl Esparza as the royal couple at the heart of Shakespeare's romance.
